detailed_summary: This paper introduces Majorana-Pauli stabilizer codes, a new class of exactly solvable fermionic lattice models that combine generalized Pauli operators with Majorana operators. The authors construct an explicit stabilizer realization of the fermionic toric code, an intrinsically fermionic Z2 topological order in (2+1) dimensions, using Z8 Pauli operators coupled to Majorana modes. Within this framework, anyons, string operators, fusion rules, and braiding statistics emerge naturally from the stabilizer algebra. The work further embeds the fermionic toric code into a duality web generated by anyon condensation and gauging of bosonic or fermion-parity symmetries, connecting bosonic topological orders, symmetry-enriched topological phases, and both bosonic and fermionic symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. The construction is shown to extend to all Abelian fermionic topological orders with gapped boundaries and all supercohomology fermionic SPT phases in (2+1)D. Additionally, the authors introduce fermionic clock and shift operators to construct an exact bosonization map for Z_D^F symmetries with D even, and realize a stabilizer model for a nontrivial Z_8^F fermionic SPT phase with no free-fermion analog.
key_contributions: Introduction of Majorana-Pauli stabilizer codes as a systematic framework for exactly solvable fermionic lattice models.
Explicit stabilizer construction of the fermionic toric code using Z8 Pauli operators and Majorana modes, with full anyon data derived from stabilizer algebra.
Establishment of a duality web connecting fermionic topological orders, bosonic topological orders, SET phases, and SPT phases via anyon condensation and symmetry gauging.
Extension of the construction to all Abelian fermionic topological orders with gapped boundaries and all supercohomology fermionic SPT phases in (2+1)D.

Introduction of fermionic clock and shift operators and an exact bosonization map for Z_D^F symmetries (D even), enabling a stabilizer model for a nontrivial Z_8^F fermionic SPT phase beyond free fermions.
methodology_analysis: The paper employs a stabilizer formalism extended to include Majorana operators, building on the Pauli stabilizer framework. The key innovation is the coupling of Z8 Pauli operators (generalized qudits) with Majorana modes to realize intrinsically fermionic topological orders. The authors define stabilizer groups that include both Pauli and Majorana operators, ensuring the algebra yields the correct fermionic parity and anyonic statistics. They derive the anyon theory (fusion rules, braiding) directly from the stabilizer algebra, avoiding the need for explicit wavefunctions. The duality web is constructed using standard techniques of anyon condensation and gauging symmetries, but applied within the stabilizer language. For the bosonization map, fermionic clock and shift operators are defined as products of Majorana operators, and the map is shown to be exact for even D. The construction of the Z_8^F SPT phase uses these operators to build a stabilizer Hamiltonian whose ground state is a nontrivial SPT state.
results_analysis: The main result is the explicit stabilizer model for the fermionic toric code, which is an intrinsically fermionic Z2 topological order. The anyon content includes a fermion e, a boson m, and a fermionic composite ψ = e × m, with nontrivial braiding statistics (e.g., π phase when braiding e around m). The duality web shows that the fermionic toric code is related to the bosonic toric code via anyon condensation of the fermion, and to other phases via gauging. The extension to all Abelian fermionic topological orders implies that any such order can be realized as a stabilizer code, generalizing the Kitaev toric code construction. The bosonization map for Z_D^F symmetries is exact for even D, and the Z_8^F SPT phase is shown to have no free-fermion analog, indicating a genuinely interacting fermionic SPT phase. Specific numbers: the construction uses Z8 (i.e., D=8) Pauli operators; the fermionic clock and shift operators are defined for even D; the SPT phase is for Z_8^F symmetry.
strengths: Provides a systematic and exactly solvable framework for fermionic topological orders, extending the powerful stabilizer code paradigm to intrinsically fermionic phases.
The explicit construction of the fermionic toric code and the derivation of anyon data from stabilizer algebra is elegant and pedagogically valuable.
The duality web unifies a wide range of topological and SPT phases within a common stabilizer description, revealing deep connections.
The bosonization map and construction of a nontrivial Z_8^F SPT phase without free-fermion analog demonstrate the power and novelty of the approach.
limitations: The construction is limited to Abelian fermionic topological orders; non-Abelian cases are not addressed.
The stabilizer models require large local Hilbert spaces (e.g., Z8 qudits) which may be challenging for physical realization.
The paper does not discuss error correction properties or fault-tolerance of the Majorana-Pauli stabilizer codes, which is a natural next step.
connections_to_research: This work directly advances the understanding of fermionic topological phases, a core interest in quantum physics. It provides a concrete lattice realization of intrinsically fermionic topological order, bridging the gap between bosonic stabilizer codes and fermionic systems. The duality web connects to symmetry-enriched topological phases and SPT phases, which are active areas of research. The bosonization map and fermionic clock operators offer new tools for studying fermionic symmetries and phases. The results are relevant to quantum error correction, as stabilizer codes are central to that field, and the extension to fermionic codes may inspire new error-correcting codes for Majorana-based qubits.
overall_assessment: This is a significant and novel contribution to the field of topological phases and quantum error correction. The introduction of Majorana-Pauli stabilizer codes provides a powerful framework for systematically constructing exactly solvable fermionic lattice models. The explicit realization of the fermionic toric code and the duality web are elegant and unifying. The extension to all Abelian fermionic topological orders and supercohomology SPT phases demonstrates broad applicability. The paper is technically rigorous and well-written, with clear derivations. While limited to Abelian orders and requiring large local Hilbert spaces, the work opens up new directions for fermionic stabilizer codes and their applications in quantum information and condensed matter physics.
